items.title: Albert Jiles Interview, 1961-02-24
items.q: I thought maybe that song had something to do with Marcus Garvey, you know.

ctx.x: No bass, piano? No piano player. I see. Well that's the first band I started playing with. After my uncle took me to Old Man's Shalow there. That was the first band. And on the way from that house I met Chris Kelly, he was playing Lawn Party and Faye Soda drummer, that was a guy I admired too, was a great drummer. And he asked me to help him carry his drum while he was playing. And so I was telling him, I was going to less and taking up drums. I'll let you work out tonight. So I got on the drum and started…
I thought maybe that song had something to do with Marcus Garvey, you know. No. Because he was a Jew maker too, you know.

Yeah he was. Well, that's a lot of different in that, that I think I can kind of understand what you mean. That he was going to build ships and take the people back. But no, that was different. When this came up about those Jew makers didn't have any passports, this was at the time before that, Martha Garvey had what they call a store line club. Well that was altogether different.
